{
  "subtype": "exploratory_data_analysis",
  "focus_variable": "state_declined",
  "per_column": [
    {
      "name": "is_declined",
      "role": "restatement",
      "is_predictor": false,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": false,
      "rationale": "This is a direct binary restatement of the focus variable (declined vs not). It reproduces the outcome itself, not an external associational variable to compare against it."
    },
    {
      "name": "expense_amount_bucket",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Buckets the continuous amount into High/Medium/Low, giving well-separated, interpretable categories that can be segmented and compared against decline rates. A genuine exploratory relationship."
    },
    {
      "name": "category_type",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Groups expenses into a few clear, interpretable category types (Hardware, Travel, Software/Services, Other) that support comparing which kinds of expenses tend to be declined. Directly serves the query."
    },
    {
      "name": "dept_decline_rate",
      "role": "restatement",
      "is_predictor": false,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": false,
      "rationale": "This is the decline rate computed per department, i.e. it bakes the focus outcome directly into the values. Comparing decline against a decline-rate is circular; it also gives fine-grained numeric scores rather than an interpretable external segmentation like department itself would."
    }
  ],
  "n_predictors": 2,
  "relationship_informativeness": 0.5,
  "rationale": "Two of the four columns (expense_amount_bucket, category_type) are strong exploratory variables: external, well-segmented, and directly enabling comparison of what gets declined. However, is_declined merely restates the focus outcome, and dept_decline_rate is a leakage/restatement of the focus aggregated by department (circular for testing decline). Notably, the query asks about differences BY DEPARTMENT, yet no clean interpretable department segmentation was added (department already exists, but the added dept_decline_rate encodes the outcome rather than a comparable predictor). As a set, the informative-relationship coverage is only partial."
}
